With participants in the "Bear Creek" sector (Area 4) of the Boulder Christmas Bird Count: Ted Floyd, Hannah Floyd, Andrew Floyd, Carl Bendorf, Megan Jones Patterson, Mike Patterson, Christa Torrens, Michael Baird, Catherine Labio, Ryan Bushong, Jack Bushong, Steve Bushong, Sandy Ramsey, Ben Ramsey, Gillian Brown. Clear and cold at start: 23 degrees Fahrenheit, but warming rapidly after sunrise, with temp maxing at 59 degrees Fahrenheit. Water bodies mostly frozen, but also with sufficient open water for various aquatic species; a tiny bit of snow in places, but basically no snow cover. Skies clear all day, wind practically non-existent; nearly perfect conditions for birding. Distance does not include extensive backtrack coverage at all sites; lunch break included within the 10 hours (but we did look at feeder birds from time to time!).----NOTES ON COVERAGE (for next year's CBC): I think we've got the morning nicely figured out; I also think we could spend more time in the Fairview High School area; and I think we spend too much time in the afternoon at the CU-South campus, mostly because the area is quite heavily trafficked by early afternoon. Consider birding more along Skunk and especially Bear creeks in town; also maybe the neighborhood west of Mohawk, south of Baseline (feeders, conifers, etc.). If it's crystal clear (as it was today), arrive 15+ min. earlier for owling; I think we were simply too late this morning for the Great Horneds. Also, spend more time in the ditch at the beginning of the long haul out to the marshes (do this on the walk back).
